msg.content:
<document>
<title>List of Nobel laureates in Physics</title>
<fragment>

The Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to 224 individuals as of 2023.[5] The first prize in physics was awarded in 1901 to Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, of Germany, who received 150,782 SEK. John Bardeen is the only laureate to win the prize twice—in 1956 and 1972.


William Lawrence Bragg was the youngest Nobel laureate in physics; he won the prize in 1915 at the age of 25. He was also the youngest laureate for any Nobel prize until 2014 (when Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize at age 17).[6] The oldest Nobel Prize laureate in physics was Arthur Ashkin who was 96 years old when he was awarded the prize in 2018.[7]


Only five women have won the prize: Marie Curie (1903), Maria Goeppert-Mayer (1963), Donna Strickland (2018), Andrea Ghez (2020), and Anne L'Huillier (2023).[8] Before L'Huillier, each woman only ever received a quarter share of the prize, although Marie Curie did receive an unshared Nobel prize in chemistry in 1911. content.content:
We need list of Nobel Prize in Physics laureates 2010-2015 inclusive, with names and brief description. I can retrieve from memory or verify via web. Probably okay from knowledge. But ensure correct. Let's recall:

2010: Andre Geim, Konstantin Novoselov — for groundbreaking experiments regarding the two-dimensional material graphene. Actually award for "groundbreaking experiments regarding the two-dimensional material graphene".

2011: Saul Perlmutter, Brian P. Schmidt, Adam G. Riess — for the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the Universe through observations of distant supernovae.

2012: Serge Haroche, David J. Wineland — for ground-breaking experimental methods that enable measuring and manipulation of individual quantum systems.

2013: François Englert, Peter W. Higgs — for the theoretical discovery of a mechanism that contributes to our understanding of the origin of mass of subatomic particles, and which was confirmed through the discovery of the Higgs boson.

2014: Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano, Shuji Nakamura — for the invention of efficient blue light-emitting diodes, which have enabled bright and energy-saving white light sources.

2015: Takaaki Kajita, Arthur B. McDonald — for the discovery of neutrino oscillations, which shows that neutrinos have mass.

We need brief description one to two sentences. Provide list per year.

We should verify maybe 2014 laureates: Yes Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura.

All good.

Provide answer.

content:
**Nobel Prize in Physics – Laureates (2010 – 2015)**  

| Year | Laureates | Contribution (brief description) |
|------|-----------|-----------------------------------|

| **2011** | **Saul Perlmutter** (USA), **Brian P. Schmidt** (USA) & **Adam G. Riess** (USA) | Recognized “for the discovery of the **accelerating expansion of the Universe** through observations of distant supernovae,” which implied the existence of dark energy. |

| **2014** | **Isamu Akasaki** (Japan), **Hiroshi Amano** (Japan) & **Shuji Nakamura** (USA/Japan) | Recognized “for the **invention of efficient blue light‑emitting diodes (LEDs)**,” which made possible bright, energy‑saving white lighting and displays. |
| **2015** | **Takaaki Kajita** (Japan) & **Arthur B. McDonald** (Canada) | Awarded “for the **discovery of neutrino oscillations**, which shows that neutrinos have mass and can change flavors, reshaping our understanding of particle physics.” |
